extracted.intended_audience: fiction/creative writers looking to overcome a stalled or stuck story
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive list of techniques and maneuvers writers can use to get past a stalled scene, chapter, or novel by altering plot, character, structure, or process. Focuses on practical, often dramatic interventions to restore momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive Outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the pressure off; create or redo outlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make an outline after or during a stuck point to clarify structure, reveal missing beats, and reduce decision pressure so you can move forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roadblocks & Obstacles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce complications or obstacles that impede goals to create conflict, force choices, and sustain narrative drive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify Character Perspective
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change POV or narrating character for scenes to reveal new information, alter tone, and renew interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalibrate Motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand what characters want and need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify characters' wants, needs, and stakes; use those forces to propel action and make scenes purposeful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen Supporting Cast
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop secondary characters with own agendas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give minor characters distinct goals and conflicts so they create friction, complicate the protagonist's path, and enrich the story world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce New Characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in new figures who introduce conflict, information, or relationships that change dynamics and reopen narrative possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fix Plot Gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify missing bridges and fill them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate logical or causal holes in the plot and add connective scenes, reveals, or beats so progression feels earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add Subplots
rubrics_metrics.description: Distract from and energize main plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce side arcs that complement or complicate the main story to provide variety, deepen characters, and sustain momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Non-Linear Elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ structural devices (flashbacks, dreams, hallucinations) to reveal backstory, offer perspective shifts, or vary pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce Mystery
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant unanswered questions for gravitational pull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed mysteries or unanswered questions that compel readers to keep turning pages and give the narrative a forward engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steal Protagonist Assets
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strip the protagonist of advantages (tools, info, relationships) to force new problems, creative responses, and stakes recalibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint Twist
rubrics_metrics.description: Reveal someone isn't who they claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce a reveal around the story midpoint that reframes relationships or goals and injects fresh tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Betrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a character betray the protagonist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use betrayal to upend trust, create emotional fallout, and complicate motives and alliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrets & Lies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use secrecy, withheld truths, or deception as sources of dramatic tension and plot propulsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kill Important Characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider character death to increase consequences and urgency—but apply it purposefully so it advances theme or plot rather than shock for shock's sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ill-Advised Romance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair unlikely or ill-timed romantic entanglements to create conflict, complicate loyalties, and generate new obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constant Peril
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep threats, deadlines, or danger present to sustain tension and maintain reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise Stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate what characters stand to lose or gain to heighten urgency and investment in outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activate Protagonist
rubrics_metrics.description: Shift from passive sufferer to active agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the protagonist agency, choices, and active pursuit of goals so the plot is driven by character decisions rather than happenstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triple Axis Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical danger + emotional stakes + philosophical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Layer conflicts across physical, emotional, and thematic/philosophical dimensions for richer, multidimensional tension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine Ending
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick an ending or endpoint to guide scene choices and plot decisions; working backward from a destination can unblock stalled narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: "What If?" Brainstorm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rapid 'what if' questioning to produce many divergent possibilities; choose the most provocative to pursue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace Chaos
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take bold, unexpected structural or tonal risks to jolt the story out of stagnation and discover new directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete Significant Sections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut scenes, chapters, or passages that bog down the story; ruthless editing can refocus momentum and reveal a leaner path forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Push Through Resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Write past gaps; solve problems later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep writing even when unsure; produce material to work with and defer perfecting solutions to revision rather than stalling progress.
